item.title: U. Iowa student allegedly assaults GOP lawmaker at DEI hearing. She denies it.
item.description: University of Iowa grad student Abigail Escatel denied assaulting GOP Rep. Steve Holt during a hearing Monday on a bill restricting DEI in higher education.

item.title: Syracuse faculty demand ‘transparency’ after false reports of ICE on campus
item.description: Why didn't the school tell everyone that ICE was not on campus, professors wonder.

item.title: UT Austin to merge gender, African, Latina/Latino studies departments
item.description: UT Austin is merging several departments, including women’s, gender, and African studies. President Jim Davis cited factors like academic mission and resource allocation. However, one professor condemned the move as an "authoritarian takeover."

item.title: U. Washington professor examines ice (not ICE) through lens of colonialism and race
item.description: Jen Rose Smith, a geography professor at the University of Washington, explores the interplay of colonialism, race, and indigeneity in her new book, "Ice Geographies." Through critical analysis, she examines ice as a racialized space, integrating themes from Native, Black, and ethnic studies into her discourse on the politics surrounding ice and its cultural representations.

item.title: Oklahoma State professor: Bad Bunny a sensation due to ‘gentrifying’ black music
item.description: The selection of Bad Bunny for Super Bowl 60's halftime show sparked controversy, in part from Oklahoma State's Lawrence Ware, who argues Bunny has appropriated reggaetón from its Black origins. Ware claims this musical gentrification makes the genre more marketable to a predominantly white audience, sidelining its Black pioneers and heritage.

item.title: Teachers ousted, disciplined over pro-ICE social media comments
item.description: Teachers faced backlash for pro-ICE social media comments, leading to resignations and administrative leave. In West Chicago, a PE teacher resigned after support for ICE sparked community protests, while in Watsonville, a special ed teacher's similar remarks prompted calls for her dismissal.
